messages.content:
A regular hexagon with side length 4 is subdivided into a lattice of 96 equilateral triangles of side length 1. Let $S$ be the set of all vertices of this lattice. Compute the number of nondegenerate triangles with vertices in $S$ that contain the center of the hexagon strictly in their interior.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We use a triangular-lattice coordinate system centered at the hexagon’s center \(O\).  
A lattice point is represented by an integer pair \((x,y)\) in the usual axial coordinates for a \(60^\circ\) triangular lattice. The hexagon of side length \(4\) is

\[
\{(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2: |x|\le 4,\ |y|\le 4,\ |x+y|\le 4\}.
\]

It has \(61\) lattice vertices, including the center.

A triangle containing the center strictly in its interior cannot have two vertices on the same ray from \(O\), nor two vertices on opposite rays. Thus we first group the \(60\) non-center vertices by their ray from \(O\).

In each \(60^\circ\) sector, the rays and the numbers of lattice vertices on them are, in angular order:

\[
4,\ 1,\ 1,\ 2,\ 1,\ 1.
\]

Indeed, in the first sector the primitive directions are

\[
(1,0),\ (3,1),\ (2,1),\ (1,1),\ (1,2),\ (1,3),
\]

and the numbers of lattice points on those rays are respectively

\[
4,\ 1,\ 1,\ 2,\ 1,\ 1.
\]

So there are \(36\) rays, with weight sequence

\[
a=(4,1,1,2,1,1)
\]

repeated six times around the center.

Index the rays \(0,1,\dots,35\) counterclockwise. Because the pattern repeats every \(60^\circ\), ray \(i+18\) is exactly opposite ray \(i\). For three distinct rays, the center is strictly inside the triangle iff the three clockwise index gaps are all strictly less than \(18\), i.e. all at most \(17\).

Let \(d_1,d_2,d_3\) be the clockwise index gaps for a valid triangle. Then

\[
d_1,d_2,d_3\in\{1,\dots,17\},\qquad d_1+d_2+d_3=36.
\]

For fixed \(d_1,d_2\), the sum of the products of ray weights over all starting rays is periodic with period \(6\). Define

\[
P(c,e)=\sum_{r=0}^5 a_r a_{r+c} a_{r+c+e},
\]

where subscripts are taken modulo \(6\). The values are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccc}
c\backslash e & 0&1&2&3&4&5\\\hline
0&76&28&28&52&28&28\\
1&28&18&24&24&18&28\\
2&28&24&18&24&28&18\\
3&52&24&24&52&24&24\\
4&28&18&28&24&18&24\\
5&28&28&18&24&24&18
\end{array}
\]

Let \(N(c,e)\) be the number of valid pairs \((d_1,d_2)\) with \(1\le d_1,d_2\le17\), \(d_1+d_2\ge19\), and residues \(d_1\equiv c\), \(d_2\equiv e\pmod 6\). Counting these gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccc}
c\backslash e & 0&1&2&3&4&5\\\hline
0&1&3&3&3&3&3\\
1&3&3&3&3&3&3\\
2&3&3&3&3&3&6\\
3&3&3&3&3&6&6\\
4&3&3&3&6&6&6\\
5&3&3&6&6&6&6
\end{array}
\]

For each valid ordered gap pair, summing over the \(36\) starting rays gives \(6P(c,e)\). Each unordered triangle is counted exactly three times, once from each vertex, so the desired number is

\[
2\sum_{c,e} N(c,e)P(c,e).
\]

Computing the sum:

\[
\sum_{c,e} N(c,e)P(c,e)
=568+420+474+744+618+672
=3496.
\]

Therefore the number of nondegenerate triangles is

\[
2\cdot 3496 = 6992.
\]

\[
\boxed{6992}
\]
